methods.name: index_momentum
methods.description: The thesis's index sleeve: hold `symbol` while its 12-month return is positive (checked monthly), otherwise cash.
methods.status: proven as crash insurance
methods.evidence_summary: SPY 1994-2026: 10.6%/yr vs 10.8% buy & hold, worst drop -34% vs -55%; robust across periods, markets and costs. Cost ~1%/yr in 2014-2026 (fast rebounds).

amendments.proposal: Replace the SPY-only momentum sleeve with index rotation: each month hold the top 1-2 of SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, EFA, EEM by 12-month return (only if positive, else cash).
amendments.rationale: Compare other major indices instead of only SPY; capture leadership shifts (e.g. emerging markets, small caps).
amendments.author: you
amendments.evidence: Backtested 2004-2026 in research/INDEX_ROTATION.md: same Sharpe (0.60 vs 0.58) at higher volatility, walk-forward 8.3%/yr (Sharpe 0.45) vs live 10.2% (0.61), desk Sharpe 0.86 vs 0.89. Claude recommends reject; awaiting your decision.

amendments.proposal: Rotate into the best-performing indices and avoid the worst: hold all but the 1-2 weakest of SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, EFA, EEM (positive momentum only), optionally rank-weighted toward the leaders.
amendments.rationale: Follow index leadership while staying diversified; avoid laggards rather than betting on one winner.
amendments.author: you
amendments.evidence: Backtested 2004-2026 (research/INDEX_ROTATION.md, follow-up): Sharpe 0.54-0.58 vs live 0.58, fragile to lookback and to removing QQQ, walk-forward 8.0%/yr (0.44) vs 10.2% (0.61), desk Sharpe 0.84-0.85 vs 0.89. Claude recommends reject; awaiting your decision.

amendments.proposal: Replace the 30% SPY momentum sleeve with the overnight sleeve (20 strongest 12-month overnight earners, held close to open, re-picked monthly), keeping 50% quality screen + 20% momentum - a higher-conviction desk.
amendments.rationale: Owner's request 2026-10-21: 'change the SPY momentum sleeve for the overnight trade - high conviction desk'.
amendments.author: you
amendments.evidence: Accepted by the user 2026-10-21 ('Swap now') after the backtest (research/DESK_OVERNIGHT.md: 18.6%/yr, Sharpe 0.98, worst -26.8% at 0.02% costs vs 16.5%, 0.91, -24.2%; break-even ~0.03%). Takes effect at `overnight activate`, once the overnight paper account works and holds ~3/7 of the desk account's equity. Implemented in the desk's own account (your choice, 2026-10-21): 50% quality, 20% momentum, 30% overnight; activated 2026-10-21.

methods.name: index_rotation
methods.description: Index rotation ("dual momentum"): each month, rank major index funds by momentum (12-month return, or a blend of lookbacks) and hold the best `top` - or, with drop_worst=N, everything except the N weakest. Only funds with positive momentum are held; a failing slot sits in cash (earning T-bills). weighting: equal slices, or "rank" (the leader gets the biggest slice). With symbols=SPY and top=1 this is index_momentum.
methods.status: tested, no edge over SPY sleeve
methods.evidence_summary: 2004-2026, 6 indices (SPY QQQ IWM DIA EFA EEM): top 2 11.6%/yr, Sharpe 0.60 vs the SPY sleeve 9.4%, 0.58 - more risk, same Sharpe; gains all from 2004-12, relies on QQQ, fragile to lookback; walk-forward 8.3% (0.45) vs 10.2% (0.61). 'Avoid the worst' (drop_worst, rank weights): Sharpe 0.54-0.58, walk-forward 8.0% (0.44). No improvement inside the desk.

methods.name: sma_crossover
methods.description: Moving-average crossover on each symbol. Each gets an equal slice (1/N of the account) and holds it while its fast average is above its slow one; a symbol that's "off" leaves its slice in cash.
methods.status: works, redundant
methods.evidence_summary: 50/200 on SPY: same insurance as momentum, near-identical results. Not in the live mix.

methods.name: pairs
methods.description: Duopoly pairs trading.
methods.status: weak
methods.evidence_summary: Duopoly pairs long/short: market-neutral but ~1%/yr above T-bills, cost-sensitive. Not in the live mix.

methods.name: quality_screen
methods.description: Top 25 of the quality stock screen, equal weight, re-picked every quarter (backtested: quarterly beat annual - research/screen_backtest.py). Positions drift between re-picks; no stop-loss (none was backtested).
methods.status: promising, not proven
methods.evidence_summary: Point-in-time 2014-2026: top 25 re-picked quarterly 17.9%/yr (Sharpe 0.89) vs same-universe 11.4% and SPY 13.8%; edge vs universe t~1.8. Survivors-only prices.

methods.name: bottleneck
methods.description: Top 8 of the bottleneck scan (python -m ai_desk bottleneck scan).
methods.status: experiment
methods.evidence_summary: Only the price-flow part is testable: 100-day MA, re-picked every 2 weeks 17.0%/yr (Sharpe 0.60, -46% worst drop) vs SPY 13.7% (0.75); an isolated best setting. Fundamental fingerprints, insider signal and theme map untested.

amendments.proposal: Replace the bottleneck sleeve's engine with plain stock momentum: the 20 large companies with the best 6-month return (skipping the latest week), above their 40-week average, re-picked every 4 weeks; optionally keep the 100-day sell rule between re-picks.
amendments.rationale: Weekly-strategy experiment (research/WEEKLY.md) found 6-12 month momentum beat the average stock in 11 of 13 years; it is simpler and better tested than the flow rotation.
amendments.author: claude
amendments.evidence: Owner chose option 2 on 2026-10-20: plain momentum (top 20 by 6-month return, above the 200-day average, re-picked every 4 weeks) WITH the 100-day sell rule between re-picks. Backtest: sleeve 19.8%/yr, Sharpe 0.76, worst drop -30%; desk Sharpe 0.92 vs 0.88. Goes live at the bottleneck sleeve's 2026-11-03 re-pick (methods.DESK_SWITCH) so current picks aren't sold early.

methods.name: momentum
methods.description: Top 20 large companies by 6-month price gain (skipping the latest week), above their 200-day average, equal weight (python -m ai_desk momentum scan).
methods.status: accepted 2026-10-20 (amendment 00e1f2b8); live from 2026-10-21 (brought forward, amendment 54b8755e)
methods.evidence_summary: 2014-2026, top 20 of the 750 largest by 6-month return, re-picked every 4 weeks, with the 100-day exit: 19.8%/yr, Sharpe 0.76, worst drop -30% as a sleeve (vs the flow rotation's 17.8%, 0.63, -45%); desk 16.5%/yr, Sharpe 0.92 vs 0.88. Survivors-only prices.

amendments.proposal: Bring the bottleneck -> plain momentum switch (amendment 00e1f2b8) forward from the 2026-11-03 re-pick to the 2026-10-21 evening run, so it trades at the 2026-10-22 open.
amendments.rationale: Owner's request 2026-10-21: 'replace bottleneck with momentum when the market opens'.
amendments.author: you
amendments.evidence: Accepted by the owner 2026-10-21. Same rules as 00e1f2b8 (backtested in research/MOMENTUM_SLEEVE.md); only the date moves. The bottleneck picks are sold about two weeks before their scheduled re-pick.

amendments.proposal: Entry filter: a stock must also be above its 100-day average to be picked (not only its 200-day), so the 100-day sell rule can't fire on the pick day; the next-ranked stocks fill the slots.
amendments.rationale: Owner's question 2026-10-21: 5 of 20 picks would be sold straight away (whipsaw).
amendments.author: you
amendments.evidence: Backtest 2014-2026 (research/MOMENTUM_ENTRY.md): entry filter 19.4%/yr, Sharpe 0.75, 92% invested vs live behaviour (sold on the pick day) 17.9%, 0.71, 86%; beat it in 8 of 13 years. Accepted by the owner 2026-10-21, from that evening's first pick.

amendments.proposal: Hold the momentum sleeve's top 10 instead of top 20 (2% of the desk each instead of 1%), keeping the live rules: above the 200 and 100-day averages to be picked, re-picked every 28 days, sold below the 100-day average. Switch at the next re-pick (2026-11-18) if accepted.
amendments.rationale: research/DESK_TOP10.md: desk Sharpe 1.06 vs 0.98 (overnight at 0.02%), +2.2%/yr, better in both halves and 11 of 13 years, holds at 3x momentum costs, worst drop unchanged (-25.6% vs -25.9%). Caveats: survivors-only prices flatter concentration; '10' was chosen after an earlier test; single-stock risk doubles.
amendments.author: you
amendments.evidence: Backtested: research/desk_top10.py -> research/DESK_TOP10.md (2014-2026 monthly, survivors-only). Desk Sharpe 1.06 vs 0.98, 90% bootstrap range of the gap +0.02 to +0.12; return gap t 3.0. Awaiting the owner's decision.

methods.name: asymmetric_bets
methods.description: Michael Sikand's 'asymmetric bets' style (Autopilot pilot), as testable rules: a stock in a hot industry, fast revenue growth, cheaper than its industry peers on price-to-sales, 30-75% off its 12-month high; hold the top 5 at 20% each, re-picked monthly.

parameters.theme: industry in top quarter by 6-month momentum

methods.status: tested, no edge (not in the live mix)
methods.evidence_summary: 2014-2026 on the 750 largest US companies: 0.4%/yr, Sharpe 0.00 vs the average stock 11.1% (0.59) and SPY 13.6% (0.81); every variant lost to the average stock. Buying 30-75% off the high cost 0.61%/month (52-week-high effect); only the industry-momentum rule helped. Survivors-only prices.

methods.name: vcp_swing
methods.description: Swing trading on VCP breakouts (Minervini's volatility contraction pattern, from the vcp-screener skill in tradermonty/claude-trading-skills) as fixed rules: a stock in a strong uptrend, a quiet tightening pause, then a breakout above its 20-day high on 1.5x volume; bought at the next open.
methods.status: tested, no edge (not in the live mix)
methods.evidence_summary: 2014-2026: 2.8%/yr, Sharpe 0.13 vs the average stock 12.1% (0.59) and SPY 13.7% (0.72); 1,123 trades, 39% winners, +0.38% per trade; loses money at 0.30% costs; no setting tested gets above 5.6%/yr. Beats random strong-trend picks, so the pattern adds a little. Survivors-only prices.

methods.name: ict_daytrading
methods.description: ICT (Inner Circle Trader) day-trading models as fixed rules on the 100 largest US companies: the Silver Bullet (5-min fair value gap after a liquidity sweep, 10-11am New York) and the Judas swing (fade a first-hour fake-out beyond the prior day's high/low), optionally with the quality score choosing the side (long strong companies, short weak ones) or a 50-day trend filter.
methods.status: tested, no edge (not in the live mix)
methods.evidence_summary: Silver Bullet (60 days, 2,974 trades): +0.01R before costs, -0.06% per trade after (t -3.5). Judas swing (3 years, 21,483 trades): -0.01R, -0.07% after costs (t -10), negative in all 13 quarters. Same as a coin-flip direction. Financial bias, long only, reaches break-even at best; trend filter worse.

methods.name: lynch_rules
methods.description: Peter Lynch's checkable rules (One Up on Wall Street, 1989): PEG under 1 (P/E / earnings growth %), the dividend-adjusted Lynch ratio (growth + yield) / P/E of 2+, growth categories (stalwarts, fast growers 18-30%), low debt, inventory not outpacing sales, no share dilution.
methods.status: tested, no edge (not in the live mix)
methods.evidence_summary: 2014-2026 point-in-time SEC data: every Lynch version made 9.2-10.6%/yr (Sharpe 0.42-0.53) vs the average stock 11.5% (0.61), SPY 13.8% (0.83) and the desk's quality screen 17.9% (0.89). PEG under 1 alone: -0.07%/quarter vs the average stock, flipping sign between 2014-19 and 2020-26. Survivors-only prices.

methods.name: short_term_effects
methods.description: Five documented short-term effects with next-open fills: weekly pullback bought at Monday's open, post-earnings drift after the 10-Q filing, the 52-week high (monthly and swing), overnight vs daytime returns, and the opening range breakout on stocks in play (60-day preview).

parameters.fills: the open after the decision close
parameters.universe: 750 largest US companies (100 for the breakout preview)

methods.status: tested, no edge as strategies (not in the live mix)
methods.evidence_summary: Pullback 11.1%/yr at 0.02% costs (Sharpe 0.49) vs the average stock 12.1% (0.59). Earnings drift: the worst-surprise fifth lags by 0.55% over 60 days (t -2.6), the best doesn't lead - a possible filter. 52-week high: lower risk, lower return. Overnight returns: +9%/yr gross, negative after costs. Breakout: negative even before costs. Survivors-only prices.

methods.name: overnight_drift
methods.description: Overnight momentum (Lou, Polk & Skouras 2019): each month take the 20 large stocks with the highest average overnight return (close to next open) over the past 12 months; hold them only overnight - buy at the close, sell at the next open - via the closing and opening auctions.

parameters.ranking: plain 12-month return (82c84226; was average overnight return)
parameters.orders: market buy at 3:55-3:59pm (market-on-close until 2026-10-21: paper filled only part), market sell at the open
parameters.regime: cash for the night when SPY < its 200-day average (7a8b29ec) or tonight's picks are down 2.0%+ since the open (9b951502, 82c84226)

methods.status: accepted as the desk's 30% sleeve (amendment 330e76e0) - live from `overnight activate`
methods.evidence_summary: Persistence out of sample: the top tenth beats the bottom by 7.3 bp a night (t 6.4, 82% of 150 months, both halves). Strategy 2014-2026: 27.7%/yr at zero cost, 15.5% (Sharpe 0.70) at 0.02% each way vs the average stock 12.6% (0.62); break-even about 0.045% each way; loses at 0.05%. Survivors-only prices.

amendments.proposal: Run the overnight drift strategy as a separate paper experiment in its own Alpaca paper account: each month lock the 20 large US stocks with the highest 12-month average overnight return; buy them market-on-close every trading day and sell everything market-on-open; log every fill against the official close/open to measure the auction cost.
amendments.rationale: research/OVERNIGHT.md: persistent (t 6.4, 82% of months), 15.5%/yr at 0.02% costs, break-even ~0.045% per trade. The open question is the real cost.
amendments.author: you
amendments.evidence: Accepted by the user 2026-10-21 ('build it'), as a paper experiment in its own account, separate from the desk. Paper fills are simulated: this tests the mechanics, not real auction costs. Superseded by 330e76e0: the sleeve runs inside the desk's account instead of a separate one.

amendments.proposal: Buy with ordinary market orders in the last minutes before the close (3:55-3:59pm New York) instead of market-on-close orders. Same picks, sizing and next-open sale.
amendments.rationale: 2026-10-21, the first night: Alpaca's paper account filled the closing-auction orders only in part - 5 of 20 in full, 5 partly, 10 not at all (expired) - so about $8,600 was invested instead of $30,000. Paper market orders fill in full; prices 1-5 minutes before the close are close to what the research assumed. Paper fills still can't measure real costs.
amendments.author: you
amendments.evidence: Owner chose 'Market orders at 3:57pm' on 2026-10-22 after the partial auction fills. Implemented as a 3:55-3:59pm window; the scheduled buy now fires at 3:54pm.

amendments.proposal: Regime checks: no overnight buys (cash for the night) when SPY is below its 200-day average, or on a day tech stocks lag defensive stocks by more than on 90% of past days (SIC groups in ai_desk/overnight_groups.json). Checked at the 3:55pm buy from prices up to then; the cut-off is refreshed by each evening run from 5 years of daily closes.
amendments.rationale: research/OVERNIGHT_REGIME.md: 2014-2026, cash on either signal (25% of nights) gave Sharpe 1.03 vs 0.70, worst drop -16% vs -36%, both halves (1.00 / 1.13). Switching into defensive or low-beta stocks instead does not help. Caveats: ~20 rules tested; survivors-only prices; part of the gain is trading less; the tech signal only works same-day, so live it is judged at 3:55pm, a few minutes before the close the backtest used; live cut-off from a 5-year window vs the backtest's expanding one.
amendments.author: you
amendments.evidence: Backtested in research/overnight_regime.py. Owner: 'Add in the checks to the overnight sleeve' (2026-10-23) after reading the results.

amendments.proposal: Replace the regime check's tech-vs-defensive test with one on tonight's own picks: cash for the night when the 20 picks' average return from today's open to 3:55pm is -1.9% or worse (the research's worst 10% of days). The SPY 200-day rule stays.
amendments.rationale: research/overnight_picks_check.py (OVERNIGHT_REGIME.md follow-up): with the SPY rule, Sharpe 1.31 vs 1.03 for the tech-vs-defensive check, worst drop -17%, both halves (1.20 / 1.45); flagged nights -12.7 / -13.9 bp. Needs no industry lists (industries and the picks change). Caveats: the sixth variant on top of ~20 rules; judged at 3:55pm not the close; fixed cut-off from the backtest (stable -1.5% to -1.9% since 2015); survivors-only prices.
amendments.author: you
amendments.evidence: Owner: 'Swap to D and merge it into main' (2026-10-23). Supersedes the tech-vs-defensive part of 7a8b29ec; its SPY 200-day rule stays.

amendments.proposal: Rank by the plain 12-month return (adjusted closes) instead of the 12-month average overnight return, and re-pick every trading day instead of monthly: the evening run ranks on that day's close, the next afternoon's buy uses it. Picks-day cut-off -2.0% (this version's worst 10%). Watchlist cohort kept monthly.
amendments.rationale: research/lookbacks.py and research/overnight_v2.py (2014-2026, survivors-only): as it would run live (ranked the evening before) with the SPY and picks-day checks, Sharpe 1.54 vs 1.31, worst drop -15% vs -17%, better in both halves (1.43/1.71 vs 1.20/1.45) and 9 of 13 years; nightly gain +1.1 bp, t 1.1 - not significant. Daily re-picking costs nothing extra (all shares are sold each morning). Caveat: this ranks momentum stocks and holds them overnight - a different idea from the researched overnight effect; only 37% of nights' picks overlap with the old ranking.
amendments.author: you
amendments.evidence: Owner: 'Change overnight to add both small improvements' (2026-10-23).

methods.name: vwap_ema
methods.description: Two intraday indicator strategies on the 100-150 largest US companies: (A) EMA9/VWAP crossover, both sides and long only; (B) Trend + Momentum + Confirmation - 20 EMA above 50 EMA, price above VWAP, volume 1.5x average, break of the previous day's or opening-range high; stop at the swing low/20 EMA, 2R target.
methods.status: tested, no edge (not in the live mix)
methods.evidence_summary: A: about zero before costs, -0.06% to -0.08% per trade after (t -10 to -12). B: negative even before costs, -0.07% to -0.14% after; random entries on the same days did better (+0.14% hourly) - the setup confirms after the move. 3R, pullback entry and no-volume variants don't help.

methods.name: minervini_sepa
methods.description: Mark Minervini's SEPA as fixed rules: Trend Template (above rising, stacked 50/150/200-day averages, near highs) + RS rating 70+, EPS +25% and sales +20% on a year earlier (SEC filings, point-in-time), a tight-base breakout entry, a 7.5% stop raised to break-even at +15%, then a 50-day exit; optional SPY 200-day market filter.
methods.status: tested: no edge (not in the live mix)
methods.evidence_summary: 2014-2026, survivors-only: full SEPA 5.2%/yr, Sharpe 0.30, worst -24% (37% invested); Trend Template alone 11.8%, 0.45, -48%; vs equal-weight universe 12.1%, 0.59 and SPY 13.7%, 0.72. Growth alone +0.52%/month vs the universe (t 2.0) is the only lead.

methods.name: tjr_model
methods.description: TJR's ICT-style index-futures day trading (NQ/ES, New York open) as fixed rules: a sweep of the prior day / Asia / London / overnight high or low between 9:30 and 11:00, a break of structure (or inverse FVG) within 30 minutes, entry next bar, stop beyond the sweep, 2R/3R/opposite-liquidity target; optional 1-hour 50-period bias.
methods.status: tested: no edge (not in the live mix)
methods.evidence_summary: 5-minute bars, 49 days, 76 trades: -0.18R to +0.05R a trade after costs (t -1.0 to 0.3), inside the random-direction range (-0.26R to +0.12R). Hourly bars, 2024-2026, 264 trades: -0.06R (t -1.3). Same result as the ICT test. His rules aren't published; discretion can't be tested.

methods.name: soros_macro_trend
methods.description: The rule-based core of George Soros-style global macro: follow each market's trend across asset classes (SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, EFA, EEM, TLT, IEF, GLD) - hold markets whose 12-month return beat T-bills; variants long/short, volatility-sized, top 3, 3-month trend. His discretionary bets aren't public or testable.
methods.status: tested: risk control, no return edge (not in the live mix)
methods.evidence_summary: 2006-2026: long-only trend 7.3%/yr, Sharpe 0.79, worst drop -9% (2008 -1%, 2022 -7%) vs SPY 11.1%, 0.67, -51% and 60/40 8.2%, 0.72, -29%; both halves. Long/short: Sharpe 0.40 (+25% in 2008).

methods.name: cameron_gap_and_go
methods.description: Ross Cameron (Warrior Trading)-style gap-and-go day trading, tested on the 750 largest US stocks (no small-cap history available): buy gap-ups at the open, sell at the close; 5-minute first-pullback entries on gap-ups.
methods.status: tested: no edge on large caps; his small-cap universe untestable here (not in the live mix)
methods.evidence_summary: 2014-2026: gaps of 4%+ -0.13% a trade after costs (t -4.1), 10%+ -0.35%; 5-minute first pullback -0.44% (144 trades). Only with hindsight (5x full-day volume) +1.5%. FTC settlement 2022 ($3m) over advertising of his results.

methods.name: leveraged_spy
methods.description: A 2x/3x S&P 500 fund (SSO/UPRO, simulated back to 1994 and checked against the real funds) traded on SPY's signals with strict risk rules: SPY above its 200-day average, leverage capped at 25% / SPY's volatility, out while the VIX is above 30, a 10% stop with a trend re-entry.
methods.status: tested: risk control works, no edge (not in the live mix)
methods.evidence_summary: 1994-2026: 3x strict 12.7%/yr, Sharpe 0.53, worst -37%; 2x strict 11.6%, 0.53, -31%; vs SPY 10.8%, 0.51, -55% and 3x buy and hold 14.9%, 0.49, -98%. 2010-2026 plain SPY was better (Sharpe 0.77 vs 0.58-0.61). Walk-forward tuning did worse than a fixed 200-day.

methods.name: drawdown_breaker
methods.description: Account-level circuit breaker (drawdown-circuit-breaker skill, tradermonty/claude-trading-skills): after a 2% day, 5% week or 8% month, no new buys (or: go to cash) until the next day / Monday / month.
methods.status: tested, no benefit; rejected 2026-10-21
methods.evidence_summary: On the desk 2014-2026 (daily): no breaker 16.4%/yr, Sharpe 0.81, worst -33.4%; freeze 15.9%, 0.79, -33.4%; go to cash 11.1%, 0.61, -35.7%. The desk buys only at re-picks, so freezing rarely matters, and cutting to cash misses the rebounds. Survivors-only prices.

amendments.proposal: Add an account-level circuit breaker to the desk: after a 2% day, 5% week or 8% month loss, block new buys (sells still go through) until the next weekday / Monday / first of next month.
amendments.rationale: From the drawdown-circuit-breaker skill in tradermonty/claude-trading-skills, reviewed 2026-10-21 at the user's request.
amendments.author: claude
amendments.evidence: Rejected by the user 2026-10-21. Backtest 2014-2026 (research/CIRCUIT_BREAKER.md): freeze 15.9%/yr, Sharpe 0.79 vs 16.4%, 0.81 without; go-to-cash 11.1%, 0.61; worst drop unchanged (~-33%).
